title: Draft invented a reset page and a timeline; the sent reply removed both

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

input.subject: Password expired - phone won't accept new one

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
My password expired, I've set a new one on the laptop, but my phone's Outlook keeps rejecting it.

Tom

conversation.author: ai
conversation.body:
Sorry to hear that.

1. Go to password.northgate.example and reset your password again.
2. Wait for IT to sync your account, which takes up to 30 minutes.
3. Restart your phone.

— Northgate IT Support

conversation.author: staff
conversation.body:
1. On your phone, sign out of Outlook and Teams.
2. Sign back in with the new password you set on the laptop.

The phone keeps the old password until you sign out, so there is no need to reset it again.

— Northgate IT Support

triage.subcategory: cached password on phone after expiry

must_include.what: Sign out of Outlook (and Teams) on the phone, then sign back in with the new password

must_not_include.what: Sends him to a reset page that does not exist
Promises a sync time no runbook gives
Tells him to reset the password again

answer.reference:

rationale: The label is what the person sent, not what the agent drafted. The draft invented a URL and a timeline (both forbidden by the reply prompt) and sent him through a second reset; the edit kept only the runbook's step 5.
